title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: Tune the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve fairness across priority classes, prevent starvation of low-traffic queues, and introduce configurable per-request and per-queue timeouts. Motivation: production incidents in Feb revealed that low-rate real-time queues could starve when large batched jobs and high-throughput background jobs arrive concurrently. This PR implements a combination of queue-weighting, time-slicing, dynamic aging, and soft timeouts so that requests bound by latency SLOs maintain predictable tail latency without sacrificing throughput.

Changes: - Add weighted fairness scheduler: per-queue weight config, proportional dequeueing to enforce share among classes. - Implement dynamic aging: pending jobs accrue aging score to boost scheduling priority over time (prevents starvation). - Introduce per-request and per-queue soft timeouts: requests exceeding timeout trigger early flush with best-effort batching policy and emit metrics. - Add queue-level tokens + bucketed queueing to reduce head-of-line blocking when large sequences are present. - Expose new config knobs in continuous_batcher/config.yaml with safe defaults for hosted and dedicated deployments. - Add metrics: continuous_batcher.queue_wait_seconds_bucket, continuous_batcher.queue_starved_count, continuous_batcher.timeout_flush_count, continuous_batcher.weight_adjustments_total. - Add end-to-end integration tests and microbenchmarks comparing baseline vs tuned scheduler under mixed workload. - Update docs/ops/continuous-batcher.md with tuning guidance and recommended defaults.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1782) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Benchmarks (mixed real-time + batch) show 95th latency improvement for RT queues and <2% throughput regression for batch - [x] Observability hooks added - [x] Backwards-compatible config defaults

Notes on behaviour: - Default weights preserve prior behavior for existing deployments (all queues weight=1). The new aging mechanism triggers after configurable grace_period (default 50ms) and linearly increases effective weight up to a cap. - Timeouts are soft: when a request hits its queue timeout we attempt an early flush to the GPU to meet latency SLO; requests may be served with smaller batch sizes. - Benchmark summary included in ci checks.

Related: ENG-1790 (follow-up to tune autoscaler interplay), SUP-4421 (customer report that triggered investigation).

ci_checks: perf-check: pass (95p rt latency improved by 22%, batch throughput regression 1.8%)
benchmarks_summary: Mixed workload bench: synthetic mix (80% RT small requests, 20% batch large requests). 95th latency for RT queues improved from 120ms -> 94ms. P99 improved from 260ms -> 210ms. Batch throughput decreased 1.8% under maximum sustained load. Overall CPU/GPU utilization comparable.
release_notes: Improve continuous-batcher scheduler to provide weighted fairness, starvation prevention via aging, and configurable soft timeouts. Adds observability metrics and tuning knobs. Default config preserves prior behavior.
notes_for_operators: Default safe config applied on main. For Dedicated customers who tuned weights at deployment time, verify config continuity. If you rely on extreme batching for maximum throughput you may want to set weight for batch queues higher or tune aging/grace_period. See docs/ops/continuous-batcher.md for recommended defaults per workload.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: small throughput regression for batch-dominated workloads (~1-3%). Mitigation: config knobs to set batch queue weight and aging cap, revert flag continuous_batcher.flags.enable_fairness=true/false, and a targeted canary rollout (10% then 50% then 100%).
